title: Arrays & Methods
definition: An ordered, integer-indexed collection of values. JavaScript arrays can hold mixed data types and dynamically resize themselves.
simpleExplanation: An array is a list of items kept in a specific order, like a grocery list. Item 0 is milk, Item 1 is bread. You can easily add items to the end (`push`), remove from the end (`pop`), or loop through all of them (`forEach`).
realWorldExample: Storing a list of a user's recent transactions, and using `array.reduce()` to calculate the total sum of their expenses.
useCases: Iterating and transforming lists of objects

basic: What is the difference between `map` and `forEach`?
intermediate: What is the difference between `slice` and `splice`?
advanced: Why is sorting an array of numbers `[1, 10, 2].sort()` dangerous in JS?

answers.question: map vs forEach?
answers.answer: `forEach` executes a function on every item but returns `undefined` (used for side effects). `map` executes a function on every item and returns a brand NEW array with the transformed items (used to modify data without mutating the original).

answers.question: Why is [1, 10, 2].sort() dangerous?
answers.answer: Because the default `.sort()` method converts all elements to Strings and sorts them alphabetically. Alphabetically, '10' comes before '2'. So the array becomes `[1, 10, 2]`. To fix this, you must provide a compare function: `arr.sort((a,b) => a - b)`.
